items.statement: Delay in Q4 FY26 financial results due to detailed audit process and additional reviews from branch consolidation
items.quote: The delay was only due to the procedural and audit related requirement. As our business has grown, the audit process has become more detailed and require additional reviews.

items.statement: Trade receivables of INR26 crores as of March FY26, with INR17.5 crores not yet due under standard 60-day credit terms
items.quote: As of the INR26 crores that we see on the books as trade receivables as of March, about 17.5 of those are not due, which means we've billed them but the credit period, standard credit period of 60 days is not yet over.

items.statement: Collection cycle of 60 to 90 days, with most receivables realized by the time of the call
items.quote: 60 to 90 days is our general cycle of collection. So around 70 to 75 days is when we actually see the realization. Most of them would have now realized by now.

items.statement: Promoter shareholding remains at 63.33%
items.quote: On the liability front, we -- the promoter shareholding remains at 63.33% and remaining has been contributed by corporate retails and others.

items.statement: GTPL Hathway entered into a business transfer agreement to acquire the digital business of 7 ACT Group companies for INR 36.23 crores cash consideration, expected to close by 15th September 2026.
items.quote: GTPL Hathway entered into a business transfer agreement to acquire the digital business of 7 ACT Group companies for an aggregate cash consideration of INR 36.23 crores and which is expected to get completed by 15th September 2026.

items.statement: Promoters did not participate in the completed buyback programme.
items.quote: As committed, the promoters did not participate in the buyback programme.

items.statement: Company is debt-free with cash and bank balance of Rs. 17 crore as on 30th June 2026
items.quote: From a balance sheet perspective, the company remains debt-free, with a cash and bank balance of Rs. 17 crore as on 30th june 2026.

items.statement: Trade receivables increased from INR60 crores to INR82 crores due to large ESG and premix orders dispatched in Q4 FY26, now normalizing
items.quote: So, as you are aware, we have three segments, and one segment is the ESG segment. So, we have a couple of large orders that were dispatched in the last quarter of the financial year, including the third quarter of the last financial year. So that has part of the receivables you can closing.

items.statement: Balanced 75% consideration against warrant issues on preferential basis was received, resulting in conversion into equity shares and strengthening capital base.
items.quote: During the quarter, the balanced 75% consideration against warrant issues on preferential basis was also received, resulting in their conversion into equity shares and further strengthening our capital base.

items.statement: Promoters recently converted partly paid shares into fully paid shares; future promoter dilution plans depend on future developments.
items.quote: The promoters have currently acquired, recently they have converted some partly paid shares into fully paid shares. So, as such, we are still thinking. It all depends on what happens in the future. It's a thing which we cannot answer right now.

items.statement: Internal auditor is Monika Garg, a veteran CA with 13-14 years experience; management expects stability and may add a larger audit firm in future
items.quote: Currently Monika Garg is our auditor who's take care of indeed. Now she is Veteran in Chartered Accountant with firm itself and been into the industry for almost 14, 13 and 14 years' experience.

items.statement: Paid-up capital is INR93 crores; management expects it to exceed INR250-300 crores by FY30 through internal accruals, promoter deployment, or preferential shares
items.quote: I think we should be more than when we have INR3,000 crores are paid up capital should be more than INR250 crores, INR300 crores.

items.statement: Debtor days expected to streamline to 60-70 days this financial year from current 200 days
items.quote: If you actually do a deep dive in the annual report, you will be seeing that from the core business which you're doing, the payments we are receiving is under 60 days.

items.statement: Debt closed at INR 311 crores and inventory at INR 348 crores for Q1 FY27
items.quote: We are at INR 311 crores. No, we closed the quarter at INR 311 crores.

items.statement: Net cash balance of INR270 crores as of June 2026
items.quote: So the INR270 crores.

items.statement: First tranche of 52 crores fundraise finalized, money expected in August; second tranche around March after demerger in standalone copper unit
items.quote: So, we have just finalized the first round of raising, at 52 crores, which is finalized, and the money should be in the bank in the month of August. The second tranche will probably be around March, after the demerger is done, in the standalone copper unit.

items.statement: Restructuring: new wholly owned subsidiary Tieramet Limited to hold copper business; Bhagyanagar Copper to merge with Bhagyanagar India; Tieramet to be demerged; NCLT hearing scheduled for 7th August
items.quote: We are going to form a new company called Tieramet Limited, which will be a wholly owned subsidiary of Bhagyanagar India. All the copper business will move from Bhagyanagar Copper to Tieramet and then Bhagyanagar Copper will be merged with Bhagyanagar India, while Tieramet is demerged outside.

items.statement: Management plans to raise INR100 crores via preference shares by September or October to support growth
items.quote: And we are in a process of raising the capital. By September or latest by October, we will raise INR100 crores to for to manage our further growth and expansion.

items.statement: Trade receivables rose to INR100 crore in Q1 FY27 due to seasonal sales booking; over 40% recovered by July-August and 90% expected by October-November.
items.quote: Trade receivables have increased because our sales have -- usually our sales are booked in Q4 and Q1. So, that is why the trade receivables in that quarter increased. But now, out of the INR100 crores more than 40% has been recovered by July and August. By October - November, 90% of the receivables will be recovered

items.statement: Management confirmed no related-party transactions with Birla Cellulose despite being in the same industry.
items.quote: No, we do not have, because anyway, we report any related party transaction, but we do not have any transactions with them.

items.statement: Days sales outstanding increased from 58 to 129 days due to slow government approval processes
items.quote: So, typically the governments we all know are a little bit slow in approval processes. So, over the past years we have mastered that art that our liquidity and our work in progress are all aligned considering this delay that happens.
